REGIS REPORT

25 March 2025

The Bangko Sentral (BSP) made significant revisions to its balance of payments (BOP) and current accounts forecasts, predicting the BOP will now be in deficit this year and that CA deficit will be much larger.

 

The BSP now forecasts a BOP deficit of US$4.0bn and a CA deficit of US$19.8bn, equivalent to 0.8% and 3.9% of GDP, respectively. The BOP revisions appear been to have driven largely by expectations of a larger CA deficit, which in turn is due to a wider trade deficit.  These revisions point to a weaker PHP but other factors (global trade flows, interest rates, et al) will also come to play.

 

More below.

 

+++

 

Digital payments continue to surge into February, with transactions over InstaPay and PesoNet combining for P1.65trn, up 34% YoY. While this seemed slower than the 38% pace in January, note that Feb 2024 was a leap year (the extra day added more than 3.5%age points to the 2024 base). For 2M25, the total P3.45trn was up 36%, a shade faster than the 35.4% recorded for FY2024. Interestingly, the volume of transactions over InstaPay accelerated, up 68% YoY in February, indicating to us that people are using digital payments more often, for smaller-ticket purchases.

 

GCash/Mynt remains the dominant wallet in the Philippines. That said, banks are pushing their own “wallets” – BDO has BDOPay while BPI has Vybe – to encourage depositors to keep the funds with their bank, instead of transferring to GCash to make payments. Market share data is scarce. But the continued growth of digital payments means there’s lots of room for everyone.

 

+++

 

Jollibee (JFC PM) disclosed that is issuing new US$ bonds, which we believe are meant to refinance bridge debt used to redeem ~US$397m worth of perps early this year.

 

+++

 

Megaworld (MEG PM) is aiming to have 2m sqm of office space in its portfolio by 2030. That target implies CAGR of 5% from the current 1.48m sqm.

MACRO
BSP adjusts BOP forecasts amidst heightened uncertainties
  • The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) in a press release, projected a weaker balance of payments (BOP) position for the country in 2025-2026
    • Hinged on slower global trade and hampered investor confidence given higher uncertainty in global macroeconomic conditions (i.e., trade policy, geopolitical issues)
    • But external risks could be offset by the domestic economy's sustained growth, easing inflation, and less restrictive monetary policy
  • BSP projections for the overall BOP position and current account (both as % of GDP) for 2025 were revised from 0.4% and -2.4% to -0.8% and -3.9%, respectively
  • While the GIR is set to decrease slightly from $106bn in 2024 to $105bn in 2025
  • In summary for the rest of the BSP projections:
    • Merchandise exports after consecutive decline in 2023 and 2024 is set to recover with modest growth of 1-2%
      • Semiconductor exports to remain unchanged given global inventory shifts
    • Services exports to see 8% growth but slower than initially expected given local talent shortages and US reshoring efforts
    • Tourism activity is expected to be back to pre-pandemic levels driven by visitors from Korea and Japan
    • Overseas Filipino remittances are projected to be below long-term trend as countries that are the top sources of remittances (Saudi Arabia, Qatar, US) have been advocating for localization of their workforces
    • FDI is expected to be flat as continued elevated rates hampers capital flows to emerging economies

 

 

CONSUMER
JFC taps offshore debt market
  • In a disclosure filed to the PSE, Jollibee Foods Corp. (JFC PM) through its wholly owned subsidiary, Jollibee Worldwide Pte. Ltd., through several banks seek to issue a potential Regulation S dollar-denominated bond offer with a tenor of five years, which subject to market conditions
    • The notes are senior unsecured notes guaranteed by JFC
    • Other details (size, indicative yield, et al) have yet to be disclosed as of late
  • Proceeds from the planned offering will be for general corporate purposes and/or refinancing debt
  • Note JFC redeemed 396mn of perpetual securities in Jan 2025 so this exercise might be intended to refinance any bridge debt used to redeem them
  • The planned debt offering comes after the company in its recent FY24 briefing guided P18-21bn in capex spend given plans to open 800 stores to total its global store network to above 10,000 stores this year
PROPERTY
Megaworld to expand office portfolio to 2mn sqm by 2030
  • Megaworld (MEG PM) plans to expand its office portfolio to 2mn sqm by 2030
    • The company will spend P30bn for construction
  • As of end 2024, it had an office portfolio of 1.48mn sqm
    • Occupancy rate of 86%
  • In 2025-2026, it will complete 140,000sqm of office space
    • All of these will be in provincial areas
    • Iloilo Business Park – 77,000sqm
    • Capital Town, Pampanga – 11,000sqm
    • The Upper East, Bacolod – 9,000sqm
    • Davao Park District – 24,000sqm
    • Northwin Global City, Bulacan – 19,000sqm
  • MEG is trading at 71% discount to NAV, 0.2X FY25E P/B, and 3.1X FY25E P/E
PROPERTY
Accenture loses contracts with the US government
  • During its earnings briefing, Accenture (ACN US) said that its Federal Services business has lost contracts with the US government after recent reviews
  • Accenture is one of the largest BPO firms in the Philippines and is one of the top office tenants of major developers
MINING
Semirara declares P2/sh dividend
  • Semirara declared a dividend of P2/sh (regular: P1.25/sh and special: P0.75/sh), lower than the P3.50/sh dividend in 1H24
    • This first tranche is equivalent to a yield of 5% and a payout ratio of 43%
    • Ex-dividend date is on April 7 and payment on April 23
  • We expect SCC to pay dividends totaling P4.50/sh this year, down from last year’s total div of P6/sh
    • Consensus expects P3.80/sh for the year

 

BANKS/DIGITAL BANKS
Digital payments up 34% in Feb; transaction volumes surge

The value of payments over InstaPay (real-time, small-tickets) and PesoNet (larger, batched payments) grew 33.7% YoY in February to P1,646bn. The figure is down 8.7% MoM, though that’s rather typical following the holiday season surge. The headline growth is also slower than the 38.2% growth in January, and slower than the 40.6% posted in Feb 2024. That said, it is important to note that 2024 was a leap year (adding 3.3ppts), which likely skewed the growth figures. For 2M25, digital payments were up 36.0% YoY to P3,449bn, still slightly faster than the 35.4% in FY2024 despite the lost day.

 

For PesoNet, payments grew 26.9% YoY in February to P933bn. That’s down 11% MoM, and a slowdown from the 32% YoY posted in January. Year-to-date, the 2M total stood at P1,986bn, up 29.6% YoY, faster than the 28.5% pace in FY2024.

 

Transactions over InstaPay increased 43.6% YoY to P713bn in February. That was down 5% MoM and was slower than the 47.8% pace in January. For the 2M25, InstaPay recorded P1,464bn in payments, up 45.8.%, a shade slower than the 46.3% in FY2024. More interestingly, the volume of transactions over InstaPay surged 67.7% in February, faster than the 61.6% in January, despite having fewer days YoY. This again highlights to us the broadening out of use cases for digital transactions.

 

We reiterate that the figures only capture transactions done between platforms (eg bank-to-bank, bank-to-wallet, wallet-to-wallet, etc) and do not include transfers done within a platform (eg GCash-to-GCash, BDO-to-BDO, etc), thus massively under-reporting the true adoption of digital payments.
